claims.claim: Athanasius of Alexandria was born about 297 and died on May 2, 373.
The work Scholia in Job (Notes on Job) is attributed to Athanasius and survives in Greek.
In the Scholia in Job, Athanasius engages with the Arians (Ariomanites), using the text of Job to argue against their position that the Son of God is a created being.

Athanasius argues in the Scholia that the word 'made' (epoiesen) in Scripture is used indifferently for genuine and natural children, not only for created things, in order to refute the Arian claim that the Son is a creature because Scripture calls him 'made'.
Athanasius was known as one of the most illustrious defenders of the Christian faith and the greatest champion of Catholic belief on the subject of the Incarnation.
Athanasius was a staunch defender of Nicene orthodoxy against Arianism in the 4th century.
The work is also referred to as 'Exerpta in Job' in some sources.
